summary: Three distinct existing CI observations timed out while TLS readers awaited completion through EOF. Missing partial-byte and connection-state evidence prevents identifying the failed response state or a common cause.
root_cause: Unknown for each observation; a shared cause has not been established

observations.request: Synthetic upstream: POST /api/reject/{status}, declared 128 bytes, one opening-brace byte sent. Loop values are 408, 413 and 429; the failing value is not logged.

timeout.source_basis: tls_socket default timeout=3; this call supplies no override

observations.expected: EOF followed by matching HTTP status and fixture_{status} body.

actual.error: TimeoutError: The read operation timed out

observations.available_context: Synthetic backend source rejects from headers, writes Content-Length/Connection: close/body and sets close_connection=True. Its request logging is suppressed. The printed proxy log reports configuration/startup, without per-request response or closure evidence.
observations.cleanup: Source finally paths terminate/wait for the proxy and shut down/close/join the synthetic backend. Existing job output shows generic post-job cleanup. No fixture-specific listener count or independent process/socket audit is available in the inspected evidence.

observations.request: Public TLS POST /api/v1/login expecting 429, declared 128 bytes with one byte sent, after eight held incomplete-body requests and a 0.3s pause. Only the public iteration uses TLS.

timeout.source_basis: This denied socket is created by connect, then explicitly settimeout(3) before read_closed(denied,429).

observations.expected: EOF followed by HTTP 429, x-request-id and retry-after: 1.

actual.error: TimeoutError: The read operation timed out

observations.available_context: The direct non-proxy fixture had passed in 15.01s. Caddy logged eight 502 connection-reset errors matching the held 4/2/2 route mix around 3.31–3.33s; the fixture closes held sockets on failure. There is no per-socket correlation proving those errors caused the denied-request timeout. The server tail does not capture that response or permit count.
observations.cleanup: Existing integration output reports listeners=0 (log line 955); PostgreSQL stop was invoked. This is recorded cleanup evidence, not a fresh independent audit.

observations.request: One of eight held public-TLS incomplete requests expecting 408: four POST login, two POST passkey-login-start and two DELETE session, each declaring 128 bytes and sending one byte. The failing held index/route is not logged.

timeout.source_basis: pending.append(connect(...)) at line 82 calls open_socket(port,23) at line 22; socket.create_connection receives that timeout at line 15. The held sockets have no later settimeout override.
timeout.distinction: settimeout(3) at line 87 applies to each newly created denied socket, not the sockets in pending. No runtime gettimeout value was logged.
timeout.total_elapsed_assertion: 14 <= elapsed < 23 is a separate later total-duration assertion; it was not reached.

observations.expected: EOF followed by HTTP 408, x-request-id, request_timeout body and connection: close.

actual.error: TimeoutError: The read operation timed out
actual.partial_bytes: Not captured; only the expected-429 path opted into diagnostics

observations.available_context: The direct fixture passed in 15.01s. Reaching line 95 implies both preceding public/admin expected-429 reads returned and passed their assertions; this is source control-flow inference. The printed Caddy section has startup/configuration/storage-maintenance messages and no per-request error/closure record. Server-tail evidence does not reveal the held socket response.
observations.cleanup: Existing integration output reports listeners=0 (log line 947); PostgreSQL stop was invoked. This is recorded cleanup evidence, not a fresh independent audit.

evidence_limits: These readers assert status/body only after EOF, so a receive timeout alone cannot distinguish no response, a partial response, or a complete response lacking timely EOF.
Prior or later green runs with unchanged fixture bytes do not establish flakiness, a fixture-only defect, a shared cause or resolution.
No ignored DB test, unit count or helper acceptance substitutes for diagnosing these wire-level failures.
required_stage5_diagnosis: Obtain bounded partial status/header/body-prefix and per-case identity evidence when an authorized existing fixture fails, preserving original errors, timeouts and assertions.
Correlate application response generation, proxy forwarding and TLS/connection closure for the same request; current logs do not provide that correlation.
Distinguish synthetic-upstream behavior from real-application admission and held-body expiration. Evaluate each observation independently before testing a shared cause.
Preserve failed evidence and verify relevant cleanup; a green run alone does not close this problem.
verification_scope: Review of existing CI logs and exact source only; no manual fixture rerun. The three causes and any relationship among them remain unknown.
